title: Bridging the Gap Between Binary and Source Based Package Management in Spack
problem: Binary package managers limit configurability due to rigid ABI requirements, while source package managers are slow to compile. HPC systems need faster deployment with flexibility.
motivation: Spack is widely deployed in HPC but cannot mix binaries built separately, forcing full rebuilds when dependencies change.
method: Splicing extension to Spack that models binary compatibility and allows seamless mixing of source and binary distributions while maintaining dependency resolution flexibility.
key_novelty: Binary compatibility model for ABI-sensitive packages like MPI in HPC package managers
contributions: Binary compatibility model for HPC packages
Extension to Spack dependency resolution engine
limitations: Limited discussion of edge cases in complex dependency chains; evaluation scope not fully detailed in abstract.
